summary: Design full interactive /permissions (allow/deny rule editor) + /resume (session picker that switches the live session); nail /resume mid-session switch feasibility

research.findings:
FEASIBLE, and cheaper than expected — Low/Medium effort. The single biggest finding: the entire settings write-back BACKEND for a rule editor ALREADY EXISTS, is claude-code-parity, is unit-tested, and is already wired off-loop. All that is missing is the TUI view + the outcome plumbing (a mechanical clone of the existing WebAction pattern) + a command-table entry. No new settings-write API, no engine/protocol change.

WHAT EXISTS (backend, done):
- permission/src/persist.rs is a 1:1 port of claude-code addPermissionRulesToSettings/deletePermissionRule with full de-dup, broken-JSON-safety (never clobbers), and destination resolution:
  - persist_permission_update(&PermissionUpdate,&PermissionPaths)->Result<bool> (add a rule; idempotent; preserves all other settings keys) — persist.rs:164
  - remove_permission_update(...) — persist.rs:249, whose doc comment literally says "for the interactive /permissions delete (PERM-1)"
  - persist_workspace_directory(dir,add,dest,paths) for permissions.additionalDirectories — persist.rs:341
  - PermissionPaths{lingxi_home,cwd}+destination_path — persist.rs:52/65; PermissionUpdate{rule,destination} — update.rs:8; PermissionUpdateDestination{UserSettings,ProjectSettings,LocalSettings,Session,CliArg} — result.rs:192
- These are already CALLED off-loop today at the "allow always" prompt site: tui/src/permission_gate.rs:148-156 builds a PermissionUpdate and calls persist_permission_update into LocalSettings; PermissionPaths is constructed at every boot site (apps/cli/src/init.rs:740, apps/cli/src/control_plane.rs:1475, apps/engine-desktop/src/lib.rs:3260, client-adapter/src/permission_gate.rs:535). So the persist precedent already exists specifically for permissions — the editor does not even need the WebAction detour, though mirroring it is cleanest.
- Rule model: PermissionPolicy holds allow_rules/deny_rules/ask_rules: HashMap<PermissionRuleSource,Vec<PermissionRule>> (policy.rs:60-64). PermissionRuleValue{tool_name,rule_content}.from_rule_string/to_rule_string (rule.rs:43/81) parse/serialize the "Bash(npm run *)" wire form. Loader permission_rules_from_settings_json(raw,source) (loader.rs:66) projects permissions.{allow,deny,ask} arrays into rules — use this (or migrations::settings_update::read_settings_map) to POPULATE the editor list at open, exactly like /web seeds WebConfigSnapshot.

WHAT IS MISSING (all TUI-layer):
- /permissions is NOT in the TUI slash table (tui/src/command.rs — no "permissions"/"resume" entries). Today it routes to the command-core PermissionsHandler (commands/core/src/permissions.rs), which only shells out to $EDITOR via handle.edit_permissions_file() returning text "Edited {path} (exit {code})." — not interactive. The existing tui/src/bottom_pane/permission_view.rs is the live-tool PROMPT (allow-once/always/deny), NOT a rule editor.
- claude-code editor UX to match (components/permissions/rules/PermissionRuleList.tsx, 1180 lines): tabbed UI, TabType='recent'|'allow'|'ask'|'deny'|'workspace' (line 33); each rules tab lists rule string + PermissionRuleDescription + "From {source}"; policySettings rules are read-only ("configured by managed settings and cannot be modified", lines 146-156); select a rule -> RuleDetails Yes/No confirm -> deletePermissionRule + persistPermissionUpdate; add via AddPermissionRules.tsx/PermissionRuleInput.tsx (type rule + pick destination); workspace tab add/removes additionalDirectories.

DESIGN (mirror the WebAction template end-to-end):
1. New tui/src/bottom_pane/permissions_editor_view.rs (BottomPaneView): list rules grouped allow/ask/deny (+ optional workspace tab; the 'recent'/denials tab can be deferred). Seed from a PermissionsSnapshot built at cmd time by reading the settings files (loader::permission_rules_from_settings_json per source). Keys: arrows/Tab navigate; type-to-add a rule string; d/Enter->confirm to remove; skip/disable policySettings rows. Model on web_picker_view + web_config_view (~300-500 LOC incl tests).
2. New effect variant threaded through the SAME 4 sites WebAction uses: ViewOutcome::RunPermissionAction(PermissionAction) in bottom_pane/view.rs (alongside RunWebAction at view.rs:47); PermissionAction{AddRule{rule,dest}|RemoveRule{rule,dest}} (can wrap the existing PermissionUpdate). Map ViewOutcome->BottomPaneOutcome (bottom_pane/mod.rs) -> ChatOutcome::PermissionAction (chat_widget.rs:1921 area) -> app.rs callback on_permission_action (mirror on_web_action, app.rs:47/145) -> mode.rs closure run_permission_action (mirror apps/cli/src/mode.rs:373 on_web_action + :567 run_web_action) that calls persist_permission_update/remove_permission_update with the boot PermissionPaths and reports via TurnEvent::SystemNotice ("Added Bash(npm:*) to allow rules (local settings).").
3. Register /permissions in tui/src/command.rs with run: ChatWidget::cmd_permissions (new fn: build snapshot + self.bottom_pane.show_view(Box::new(PermissionsEditorView::new(snapshot))) — cf. cmd_theme chat_widget.rs:1259, cmd_web:1268). Slash run signature is fn(&mut ChatWidget,&str)->ChatOutcome.

LIVE-EFFECT NUANCE (must flag): the running PermissionPolicy is built ONCE at boot behind an Arc and holds a fixed rule set (policy.rs authorize_with_mode doc, lines 306-320). The allow-always path achieves live effect by ALSO pushing into an in-memory Arc<Mutex<Vec<PermissionRule>>> session_allow_rules (permission_gate.rs:144) IN ADDITION to the disk persist. So an ADD from the editor that must take effect THIS session should likewise push a session rule (only an allow-side session bucket exists today — session_allow_rules; deny/ask have no live session bucket). If we accept disk-only persistence, added/removed rules take effect on next settings reload / next session, which still matches claude-code's persistPermissionUpdate write-to-settings semantics for the file layer. Recommend: editor persists to disk (done API) AND, for allow rules, mirror the session_allow_rules push for immediate effect; document deny/ask as effective-next-load unless the session-rule mechanism is extended.
facts: permission/src/persist.rs already provides the full write-back API: persist_permission_update (add, line 164), remove_permission_update (remove, line 249 — doc says 'for the interactive /permissions delete (PERM-1)'), persist_workspace_directory (additionalDirectories, line 341). All idempotent, preserve other keys, refuse to overwrite broken JSON, and are unit-tested.

PermissionPaths{lingxi_home,cwd} + destination_path (persist.rs:52/65) and PermissionUpdate{rule,destination} (update.rs:8) with PermissionUpdateDestination{UserSettings,ProjectSettings,LocalSettings,Session,CliArg} (result.rs:192) are the ready-made types.

The persist API is ALREADY called off-loop for permissions at the allow-always prompt: tui/src/permission_gate.rs:148-156 (LocalSettings). PermissionPaths is constructed at boot in apps/cli/src/init.rs:740, apps/cli/src/control_plane.rs:1475, apps/engine-desktop/src/lib.rs:3260, client-adapter/src/permission_gate.rs:535.

There is a generic settings writer too: migrations/src/settings_update.rs update_settings(path, Vec<(key,Option<Value>)>) (line 76) + read_settings_map (line 40) + SettingsSource/settings_path — but permission/src/persist.rs is the purpose-built one to use.

Current TUI /permissions is NOT interactive: commands/core/src/permissions.rs PermissionsHandler only shells to $EDITOR via handle.edit_permissions_file() returning 'Edited {path} (exit {code}).'; and /permissions is absent from the TUI slash table tui/src/command.rs (grep for 'permissions'/'resume' returns nothing).
tui/src/bottom_pane/permission_view.rs is the live-tool PROMPT (allow-once/always/deny + ExitPlanMode + Bypass), not a rule editor — a NEW view is required.

claude-code editor = components/permissions/rules/PermissionRuleList.tsx (1180 lines): tabs recent|allow|ask|deny|workspace (line 33); lists rule string + source; policySettings rules read-only (lines 146-156); delete via RuleDetails Yes/No confirm -> deletePermissionRule + persistPermissionUpdate; add via AddPermissionRules/PermissionRuleInput; workspace tab edits additionalDirectories. Write core = addPermissionRulesToSettings (permissionsLoader.ts:229) -> updateSettingsForSource.

Outcome plumbing to clone: web_config_view.rs returns ViewOutcome::RunWebAction(WebAction) (view.rs:47) -> BottomPaneOutcome::RunWebAction -> ChatOutcome::WebAction (chat_widget.rs:1921) -> app.rs on_web_action (app.rs:47/145) -> apps/cli/src/mode.rs on_web_action:373 / run_web_action:567 (async write + SystemNotice). A PermissionAction variant threads the identical 4 sites.

Slash open pattern: SlashCommand{run: ChatWidget::cmd_*} in tui/src/command.rs; cmd_theme (chat_widget.rs:1259) uses self.bottom_pane.show_view(Box::new(ThemePickerView::new(..))); cmd_web (1268) builds a snapshot then show_web_picker. Run signature fn(&mut ChatWidget,&str)->ChatOutcome.

Populate the editor list at open via permission/src/loader.rs permission_rules_from_settings_json(raw, source) (line 66) which parses permissions.{allow,deny,ask} into PermissionRule{PermissionRuleValue{tool_name,rule_content}, behavior, source}; rule.rs from_rule_string/to_rule_string (43/81) handle the 'Bash(npm run *)' wire form.
risks: LIVE-EFFECT GAP: the running PermissionPolicy is built once at boot behind an Arc with a fixed rule set (policy.rs:306-320). Editor writes reach DISK via persist.rs but do NOT hot-reload into the live gate. The allow-always path gets live effect only by also pushing into an in-memory session_allow_rules Arc<Mutex<Vec>> (permission_gate.rs:144). For editor ADDs to take effect this session, mirror that push (only an allow-side session bucket exists today; deny/ask would be effective-next-load unless that mechanism is extended). Must document this behavior.

policySettings (managed) rules must be shown read-only and never offered for delete/persist (persist.rs already refuses non-persistable destinations Session/CliArg, but the VIEW must gate policySettings rows itself — claude-code does this in RuleDetails lines 146-156).

Destination choice: the allow-always precedent hardcodes LocalSettings; a full editor should let the user pick User/Project/Local (claude-code offers all three). Reading rules from multiple sources for display but writing to one requires a small destination picker in the add flow.

The enterprise allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly gate is intentionally NOT ported (persist.rs divergence note) — acceptable, but means the editor will persist where an enterprise claude-code would refuse.

settings.local.json .gitignore side-effect and file-watcher markInternalWrite hint are not ported (persist.rs notes) — a live settings watcher, if later added, would see the editor's write as an external change.

research.findings:
FIRM RECOMMENDATION: quit-the-current-loop + in-process re-mount via the EXISTING startup resume path. NOT a true in-place orchestrator swap, and NOT a process re-exec. On the picker's Enter, signal run_app to exit its loop carrying the chosen uuid; let run_ratatui run its normal teardown; then re-enter mount_resumed_tui(argv, uuid, load_resume_session(uuid)) which already does everything correctly (writer retarget + history seed + cost restore + scrollback replay + a fresh run_ratatui).

WHY A TRUE IN-PLACE SWAP IS INFEASIBLE / TOO RISKY (three independent blockers, all baked at BUILD time):

(1) The JSONL writer file is fixed at build. build_runtime_for_tui_inner sets cfg.session_id_override = id (apps/cli/src/init.rs:728-730) and build_runtime_from_config names the writer <id>.jsonl append-mode from that. There is NO runtime retarget-writer API. If you mid-session merely overwrite the live SessionState.session_id/history (the trick seed_orchestrator_session uses, apps/cli/src/run.rs:1538-1575) WITHOUT rebuilding the orchestrator, the writer still points at the OLD <old-id>.jsonl, so turns after the switch append to the old file under the new session_id — exactly the resume-forks-new-file / conversation-split-across-files bug recorded in memory. This alone kills in-place.

(2) The bridge channels are single-use and already moved. bridge_rx/permission_rx/turn_tx are created in build_runtime_for_tui_inner (init.rs:709-714) and wired INTO the orchestrator's BridgeOutputStream at build. run_ratatui moves bridge_rx/permission_rx into run_app once (apps/cli/src/mode.rs:483-505), where run_app stores events_rx as a RataApp field (tui/src/app.rs:308,343). Swapping to a different orchestrator would need a different receiver spliced into the running blocking loop.

(3) The effect closures capture the OLD orchestrator + OLD turn_tx. on_submit / on_switch_model / on_web_action / on_connect_action / on_bash / on_compact are constructed in run_ratatui (mode.rs:341-435) as Boxed FnMut over Arc clones of the just-built orchestrator and turn_tx, then handed to run_app via AppCallbacks (app.rs:345-352). run_app cannot rebuild those closures from inside its loop, so a swapped-in orchestrator would still be driven by the old handle. The ChatWidget also holds its own Arc<dyn OrchestratorHandle> via set_orchestrator (app.rs:375-377) for /context,/compact — another old-handle reference to re-point.

Plus in-flight-turn / cost-tracker / subscription / permission-gate all live in the old build; a safe swap requires request_exit() (closes the responses websocket, on the correct reactor) which run_ratatui ALREADY performs at loop exit (mode.rs:515). That teardown is the natural seam — re-use it rather than fight it.

WHY THE RE-MOUNT PATH IS CLEAN AND LOW-RISK: the entire proven startup resume path already exists and is exactly what one turn of a switch needs. mount_resumed_tui (run.rs:1481-1522) builds a fresh runtime with build_runtime_for_tui_inner(argv, Some(id)) (correct writer retarget), seeds history via seed_orchestrator_session, restores cost (run.rs:1504-1515), replays scrollback via tui::replay::rebuild_from_jsonl (run.rs:1520), and calls run_ratatui fresh. load_resume_session(uuid) (run.rs:1724) is the disk loader. So a mid-session /resume switch is literally: tear down current (run_ratatui already does request_exit + save_session_cost), then call the same mount_resumed_tui with the picked id. This is an in-process re-mount loop around run_ratatui — no process re-exec, no new engine API, and it inherits every resume-parity fix already landed.

WHAT THE PICKER PRODUCES: tui/src/resume.rs is a full-screen alternate-screen picker (run_resume_picker uses crate::setup_terminal, resume.rs:295-333), NOT a bottom_pane view. On Enter it yields ResumeOutcome::Resume(Uuid) (resume.rs:174-176) → run_resume_picker returns Option<Uuid>. So the value crossing the boundary is just a Uuid — perfect for a re-mount signal.

REQUIRED WIRING (small, additive): (a) new ChatOutcome::SwitchSession(Uuid) variant in tui/src/chat_widget.rs:49-91 (today Quit is the only loop-exit; app.rs:134-135 maps Quit→return Ok(())). (b) run_app must return an exit enum distinguishing Quit vs SwitchSession(uuid) instead of today's io::Result<()> (app.rs:305/326,381). (c) a thin loop at a level that HOLDS argv (run_resume / the mode dispatch, since mount_resumed_tui needs argv:&Argv) that, on SwitchSession(uuid), calls load_resume_session(uuid)+mount_resumed_tui again. NOTE: run_ratatui does not currently carry argv, so either the loop lives one level up (in run.rs, wrapping mount_resumed_tui) or argv gets threaded into run_ratatui. The picker itself can run full-screen AFTER run_app returns (reuse run_resume_picker) OR be reimplemented as a bottom_pane view that emits the uuid via BottomPaneOutcome; either works, but running the full-screen picker after the loop exits is the least invasive because it avoids nesting an alt-screen picker inside run_app's own terminal.
facts: tui/src/resume.rs is a full-screen alt-screen picker (run_resume_picker uses crate::setup_terminal, lines 295-333), not a bottom_pane view; Enter yields ResumeOutcome::Resume(Uuid) (resume.rs:141-148,174-176) and run_resume_picker returns Option<Uuid>.

Startup resume retargets the JSONL writer at BUILD time: build_runtime_for_tui_inner(argv, Some(id)) sets cfg.session_id_override=id (apps/cli/src/init.rs:728-730) → build_runtime_from_config names writer <id>.jsonl append-mode. No runtime retarget-writer API exists.

mount_resumed_tui (apps/cli/src/run.rs:1481-1522) is the full startup resume mount: build with Some(id), seed_orchestrator_session overwrites session.history/session_id/model (run.rs:1538-1575), restore_session_cost (run.rs:1504-1515), replay scrollback via tui::replay::rebuild_from_jsonl (run.rs:1520), then run_ratatui(tui_build, None, resumed_messages).
load_resume_session(uuid) (apps/cli/src/run.rs:1724-1727) is the disk→Vec<JsonlMessage> loader for a session id.

Orchestrator + its bridge channels are built once and consumed: bridge_rx/permission_rx/turn_tx created in build_runtime_for_tui_inner (init.rs:709-714), moved into run_app once (mode.rs:483-505); run_app stores events_rx as a RataApp field (tui/src/app.rs:308,343).

The effect closures (on_submit/on_switch_model/on_web_action/on_connect_action/on_bash/on_compact) are Boxed FnMut built in run_ratatui (mode.rs:341-435) capturing Arc clones of the OLD orchestrator + OLD turn_tx; handed to run_app via AppCallbacks (app.rs:345-352). ChatWidget also holds its own Arc<dyn OrchestratorHandle> via set_orchestrator (app.rs:375-377).

run_ratatui already performs the safe teardown at loop exit: summary_orch.request_exit() closes the responses websocket on the correct reactor (mode.rs:515) and save_session_cost persists cost (mode.rs:516-534), then prints the 'Session saved. Resume with: lingxi --resume <uuid>' line (mode.rs:541-543).
ChatOutcome (tui/src/chat_widget.rs:49-91) has NO switch-session variant today; Quit is the only loop-exit and app.rs:134-135 maps Quit→return Ok(()). run_app returns io::Result<()> (app.rs:326).

The 'resume forks new file' memory bug is exactly the failure an in-place session_id overwrite would reproduce: overwriting live SessionState.session_id without rebuilding leaves the writer on the old <old-id>.jsonl while new lines carry the new id, splitting the conversation across files.

mount_resumed_tui takes argv:&Argv, but run_ratatui does not currently hold argv (mode.rs:213-217) — so an in-process re-mount loop must live in run.rs (wrapping mount_resumed_tui) or argv must be threaded into run_ratatui.
risks: Terminal ownership: if the resume picker runs full-screen (run_resume_picker's own setup_terminal) it must run AFTER run_app has torn down its Terminal/TerminalSession (app.rs:337-339); nesting an alt-screen picker inside run_app's live terminal will corrupt the display. Preferred: return the switch signal, let run_app exit, then run the picker.

argv must reach the re-mount site: run_ratatui lacks argv, so either host the switch loop in run.rs around mount_resumed_tui, or thread argv into run_ratatui — otherwise mount_resumed_tui cannot be called.

run_ratatui's exit tail unconditionally prints 'Session <uuid> saved. Resume with…' and saves cost (mode.rs:516-543); on a SwitchSession exit that stdout line will scroll into the next mounted session unless suppressed for the switch arm (cost-save is fine/idempotent, but the println is user-visible noise).

In-flight turn at switch time: a running turn spawned by on_submit lives on the outer runtime; request_exit() (mode.rs:515) is the intended stop, but the picker should be blocked/deferred while a turn streams, or the switch must cancel current_turn first, to avoid a half-streamed turn writing into the old session file after the user asked to leave it.

State that does NOT auto-reset on re-mount: any process-global or argv-derived state (e.g. --resume flag, from_pr filter, permission mode) is re-read from argv on the new build; confirm the re-mount passes the SAME argv so the target session inherits the correct permission mode (build_runtime_for_tui_inner re-resolves it, init.rs:718).

research.findings:
WIRING PLAN for interactive /permissions + /resume, following the WebAction/ConnectAction precedent end-to-end. Both are currently UNregistered in the ratatui BUILTIN registry (verified: no "/permissions" or "/resume" entries in tui/src/command.rs) — they are the two remaining deferred slash commands. The existing commands/core PermissionsHandler is NOT a text listing; it opens $EDITOR via handle.edit_permissions_file() (commands/core/src/permissions.rs:33). We replace both with in-pane interactive views.

=== (1) ChatOutcome variants + app.rs arms + mode.rs closures ===
Mirror the WebAction/ConnectAction "off-loop effect" shape exactly. That precedent is a 6-file chain: ChatOutcome variant (chat_widget.rs:49-91) -> AppCallbacks Boxed FnMut field (app.rs:36-62) -> app.rs run-loop match arm invoking the callback (app.rs:134-179) -> run_app threads the closure param into AppCallbacks (app.rs:305-353) -> mode.rs builds the closure that spawns the async effect onto the live handle and reports back via TurnEvent::SystemNotice (mode.rs:373-396, bodies run_web_action/run_connect_action at mode.rs:557+). Views feed it via ViewOutcome (view.rs:19-55) -> map_view_outcome (mod.rs:388-410) -> BottomPaneOutcome (mod.rs:80-122) -> chat_widget map at chat_widget.rs:1919-1923.

PERMISSIONS is a clean 1:1 clone of that off-loop pattern. Add:
- ChatOutcome::PermissionAction(PermissionAction) — carries an Add{rule_string, behavior, destination} / Remove{...} intent (built from permission/src/update.rs PermissionUpdate = {rule: PermissionRule, destination: PermissionUpdateDestination}). Model the enum in tui/src/bottom_pane/view.rs next to ConnectAction/WebAction, and add ViewOutcome::RunPermissionAction + BottomPaneOutcome::RunPermissionAction. Reuse the exact ViewStack::apply "TEST keeps open / SAVE closes" bookkeeping (mod.rs:900-956): an add/remove keeps the editor OPEN (like /web TestSearch) so the user can make several edits; only Esc/done closes it.
- AppCallbacks.on_permission_action: Box<dyn FnMut(PermissionAction)>; app.rs arm calls it (copy the WebAction arm at app.rs:145-147).
- mode.rs on_permission_action closure: spawn onto the captured handle, call permission/src/persist.rs persist_permission_update(:164) or remove_permission_update(:249) with a PermissionPaths{lingxi_home, cwd} (persist.rs:52-82 resolves the 3 dest files: User ~/.claude/settings.json, Project .lingxi/settings.json, Local .lingxi/settings.local.json), then push the "Added/Removed rule" result back via TurnEvent::SystemNotice (identical to run_connect_action). NOTE: persist writes to the SETTINGS FILE; the LIVE in-memory PermissionPolicy is not hot-reloaded by this call — flag as a parity follow-up (claude-code also only persists; live gate reloads on next settings read). This is a pure settings write, so NO engine-handle method is strictly required, but keeping it on the handle keeps the reactor correct.

RESUME does NOT fit the pure off-loop pattern because a correct switch must REBUILD the runtime (see risks). Its ChatOutcome must UNWIND the blocking loop, not spawn a side-effect. Add:
- ChatOutcome::SwitchSession(uuid::Uuid). Change RataApp::run (app.rs:113) and run_app (app.rs:326) to return an AppExit enum { Quit, SwitchSession(Uuid) } instead of io::Result<()> (the loop currently returns Ok(()) on Quit at app.rs:135; add a SwitchSession(uuid) return in the outcome match). run_app currently returns io::Result<()> — widen to io::Result<AppExit>.
- No AppCallbacks entry and no mode.rs closure for the switch itself; instead run_ratatui's run_result match (mode.rs:535-554) gains a SwitchSession(uuid) arm. Because run_ratatui does NOT receive argv (signature at mode.rs:213 takes tui_build/registration/resumed_messages only) and the re-mount needs argv for build_runtime_for_tui_inner(argv, Some(uuid)), the switch signal must propagate one level OUT to a caller that has argv (run.rs mount_resumed_tui:1481 / the mode.rs:191 fresh-launch site). Practical shape: run_ratatui returns an enum {ExitCode(i32), SwitchTo(Uuid)}; the launch dispatcher loops: on SwitchTo(uuid) -> load_resume_session(uuid) (run.rs:1724) -> build_runtime_for_tui_inner(argv, Some(uuid)) (run.rs:1489, sets session_id_override so the JSONL writer targets <uuid>.jsonl) -> seed_orchestrator_session (run.rs:1498) -> run_ratatui again with the rebuilt runtime + rebuilt transcript (tui::replay::rebuild_from_jsonl, run.rs:1520). This exactly reuses the proven --resume mount_resumed_tui path (run.rs:1481-1521); we are just triggering it from a live session instead of process launch.

=== (2) cmd_permissions / cmd_resume methods ===
Both go in chat_widget.rs as fn(&mut ChatWidget,&str)->ChatOutcome (SlashCommand.run signature, command.rs:44-46) and call self.bottom_pane.show_view(Box::new(..)) then return ChatOutcome::Continue (identical to cmd_theme at chat_widget.rs:1257-1261 and cmd_web at 1268-1276).
- cmd_permissions: construct a new PermissionEditorView seeded with the current rule strings. Seed source: permission/src/loader.rs permission_rules_from_settings_json(raw, source) (:66) projects permissions.{allow,deny,ask} arrays into rules; read the 3 settings files via PermissionPaths::destination_path. There is NO OrchestratorHandle getter for live rules (verified — only edit_permissions_file at orchestrator.rs:695). Two seeding options: (a) preload a rules snapshot at startup into a shared Arc<Mutex<>> passed to run_app (mirrors the web_snapshot slot built at mode.rs:290-309 and threaded via run_app param app.rs:312 + set_web_snapshot app.rs:361-363, read in cmd_web at chat_widget.rs:1269-1273); or (b) read the files synchronously inside cmd_permissions via the run_core_command throwaway-block_on bridge (chat_widget.rs:1435-1442) — the files are tiny and local, so a blocking read on the render thread is acceptable, but (a) matches the /web precedent and keeps the render thread pure. Recommend (a). The view's add/remove keystrokes return ViewOutcome::RunPermissionAction; the current buckets update optimistically in-view.
- cmd_resume: ArgSpec::Optional (claude-code argumentHint "[conversation id or search term]"). With an arg, pre-seed ResumeState.query (resume.rs:81 has query/in_search_mode) so the picker opens pre-filtered. Construct a ResumeMidSessionView wrapping ResumeState (resume.rs:80-137) — REUSE the pure handle_resume_key (resume.rs:161) and resume_lines (resume.rs:217) verbatim; only adapt them into a BottomPaneView instead of the standalone alt-screen run_resume_picker (resume.rs:295). On ResumeOutcome::Resume(uuid) (resume.rs:141-148) emit ViewOutcome that maps to ChatOutcome::SwitchSession(uuid); on Cancel just close.

=== (3) command.rs BUILTIN rows ===
Add two SlashCommand entries to BUILTIN (command.rs:58), copying the /web (:91) and /connect (:99) shapes:
- {name:"/permissions", aliases:&["allowed-tools"], description:"Manage allow and deny tool permission rules", args:ArgSpec::None, advertised:true, run:ChatWidget::cmd_permissions}
- {name:"/resume", aliases:&["continue"], description:"Resume a previous conversation", args:ArgSpec::Optional, advertised:true, run:ChatWidget::cmd_resume}
The registry is the single source for completion + /help + dispatch (test-enforced registry_is_the_single_source... at command.rs:484), so adding the rows lights up the completion popup and /help automatically. Aliases match claude-code (allowed-tools / continue).

=== (4) Test strategy ===
The state/key layers are pure and already unit-tested in place — extend that pattern; assert ChatOutcome variants at the boundary rather than driving the engine.
- ResumeState is already fully covered (resume.rs:335-428: arrows/clamp/enter-uuid/esc/type-to-search/empty-state). Inside the synchronous TUI loop you cannot .await. Two viable off-loop routes:
(a) PRELOAD at startup into a shared Arc<Mutex<Vec<ResumeRow>>> passed to run_app (identical to the web_snapshot slot: built in mode.rs run_ratatui before the loop, threaded as a run_app param, stored via a set_* on the widget, read in cmd_resume). Simple, matches precedent; rows go slightly stale as new sessions are written but claude-code snapshots too. Recommend this.
(b) LAZY load off-loop: cmd_resume returns a ChatOutcome::LoadResumeRows action; a mode.rs closure spawns load_resume_rows and pushes the rows back through a new TurnEvent, and the widget then show_view the picker. More plumbing (new TurnEvent variant + a second round-trip) — only needed if staleness matters. The handle also exposes list_resumable_sessions -> Vec<(id,label)> (orchestrator.rs:859) but its label lacks the metadata_label formatting the CLI loader builds, so prefer the loader path either way.

risks: RESUME SWITCH IS NOT AN IN-PLACE SWAP: resume_session (handle_impl.rs:71) does not retarget the JsonlWriter (fixed at construction, conversation.rs:1277), so calling it live re-creates the file-fork bug from memory. The switch MUST unwind run_app and re-mount via build_runtime_for_tui_inner(argv, Some(uuid)) + mount_resumed_tui (run.rs:1481-1521). This forces a signature change: RataApp::run/run_app must return an AppExit{Quit, SwitchSession(Uuid)} enum instead of io::Result<()> (app.rs:113/326), and the signal must propagate past run_ratatui (which lacks argv, mode.rs:213) to a launch-site dispatcher loop.

No OrchestratorHandle method reads live permission rules for seeding the editor; the seed must come from reading the 3 settings files (loader.rs:66) either preloaded at startup (recommended, web_snapshot pattern) or via a blocking read on the render thread. Also persist_permission_update writes only the SETTINGS FILE — the live in-memory PermissionPolicy is not hot-reloaded by the write, a parity gap to note (matches claude-code, which reloads settings on next read).

Resumable-session rows require an async disk scan unavailable inside the synchronous TUI loop; must be preloaded into a shared slot at startup (rows go slightly stale) OR fetched via a new off-loop ChatOutcome + TurnEvent round-trip. The preload slot must be kept distinct from the startup --resume picker path (run.rs:1629) to avoid double-loading.

Re-mounting for a switch tears down and rebuilds the entire runtime (new websocket, new orchestrator, cost re-seed via restore_session_cost_usd run.rs:1507). The current session's cost is persisted on exit (mode.rs:516-534) — ensure the switch arm ALSO persists the outgoing session's cost before re-mount, or the outgoing session loses its cost, since the switch bypasses the normal Ok(Ok(())) exit arm at mode.rs:536.

Do NOT register /permissions or /resume as prompt-injecting core commands (run_core_command path, chat_widget.rs:1417) — they are interactive views, so their cmd_* must show_view directly like cmd_web/cmd_theme, not route through submit_core_prompt.

design.summary: Both commands are buildable in the ratatui TUI. /permissions becomes a real interactive rule editor: the settings write-back backend already exists and is unit-tested (permission/src/persist.rs persist_permission_update:164 / remove_permission_update:249 / persist_workspace_directory:341, driven off-loop via a mechanical clone of the WebAction pattern). /resume becomes a live in-session switch, but NOT via a true in-place engine swap — that is blocked by three build-time couplings. Instead the picker emits a signal that unwinds the blocking loop and re-mounts the runtime in-process through the already-proven startup resume path (mount_resumed_tui, run.rs:1481). Both are the last two unregistered slash commands (no /permissions or /resume in tui/src/command.rs BUILTIN, verified).
design.permissions_plan: Full interactive rule editor (see detailed permissions_plan field); backend persist.rs is done and tested, only the TUI view + WebAction-clone plumbing + BUILTIN row are new; live allow-rule effect via session_allow_rules, deny/ask effective-next-load.
design.resume_switch_decision:
FIRM: RESTART-RUNTIME via IN-PROCESS RE-MOUNT (unwind the blocking loop, rebuild the runtime through mount_resumed_tui, same OS process). NOT a true in-place orchestrator swap; NOT a process re-exec; NOT text-fallback.

Why NOT in-place swap (three independent build-time blockers, all verified): (1) The JSONL writer file is fixed at construction. build_runtime_for_tui_inner sets cfg.session_id_override then names the writer <id>.jsonl append-mode (init.rs:729). The live resume_session override (orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs:71-90) swaps history + adopts session_id + seeds last_jsonl_uuid but does NOT retarget the writer — so post-switch turns would append to the OLD <old-id>.jsonl under the new session_id, reproducing the documented resume-forks-new-file / conversation-split bug. (2) The bridge/permission/turn channels are single-use, created in build_runtime_for_tui_inner and moved into run_app once (mode.rs:483-505). (3) The effect closures (on_submit/on_switch_model/on_web_action/on_bash/on_compact) are Boxed FnMut built in run_ratatui capturing Arc clones of the OLD orchestrator + OLD turn_tx; run_app cannot rebuild them mid-loop, and ChatWidget also holds its own old Arc<dyn OrchestratorHandle> via set_orchestrator.

Why NOT process re-exec: unnecessary and strictly worse — terminal teardown/flicker, shell round-trip, loses the in-process advantage. mount_resumed_tui already performs a CLEAN in-process rebuild at startup (correct writer retarget + seed_orchestrator_session + restore cost + rebuild_from_jsonl + fresh run_ratatui) and inherits every landed resume-parity fix. Re-using that seam is the honest, low-risk path: the user experiences a genuine mid-conversation switch (same process, scrollback replayed) while the engine is safely rebuilt rather than mutated in place.
design.resume_plan: Bottom-pane picker reusing pure resume.rs logic; live switch achieved by in-process runtime re-mount (restart-runtime), NOT in-place swap and NOT process re-exec — see detailed resume_plan and resume_switch_decision fields.
